Alicia (CS): Hey team — LilacBay (tenant tb-879) opened a support ticket: p95/p99 latency regressions on text-generation since ~2026-03-12 14:00 UTC. They report p95 around 4s (was ~1.8s) and p99 up to ~12s. Affects their chat endpoint (single-user interactive flows). Putting details here for triage and repro.
Ben (Support): Thanks. Customer attached sample request and timestamps. Repro summary from them: single request, model redwood-7b-v2, prompt ~1200 tokens, temperature 0.7, streaming enabled. They said it spikes intermittently ~every 20-30 minutes. Tenant has steady qps ~8rps normally. No recent config changes on their side.
Alicia (CS): Ticket id 34219, support log excerpts below.
Ben (Support): ````
Request: POST /v1/generate
Model: redwood-7b-v2
Tenant: tb-879
Batch size: 1
Prompt tokens: ~1200
Customer observed timeline:
 - 2026-03-12T14:02:01Z request_id=r-9f4b
 - 2026-03-12T14:02:05Z token_stream started
 - 2026-03-12T14:02:17Z final token
Total latency observed ~16s (server-side reported 12.3s)
````

Ben (Support): I pulled r-9f4b from request logs and it shows long queue wait on the serving layer. Tracing link: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/r-9f4b

Sam (SRE): cc @Rita — initial glance suggests a per-host queue spike rather than model compilation. I see high tail on a single GPU host (gpu-az3-11). The host had a noisy neighbor (large embed batch job) around the same timeframe.

Rita (Infra): Looking at host metrics — that node had an embeddings batch job (customer: Cedarwood) that started at 14:00 and overwhelmed memory bandwidth, causing request queues to pile. KV cache miss rate for redwood-7b-v2 jumped from 3% -> 42% during the window. That explains extra decode time and host contention.

Alicia (CS): LilacBay insists this is a generation endpoint issue for them; they don't run embeddings. Any quick mitigations we can offer while we investigate? They asked for a temporary SLA or reservation.

Sam (SRE): Short-term mitigations we can propose:
 - Move LilacBay routing to a different pool (soft migration) — quick but requires capacity.
 - Apply a per-tenant throttling config to smooth bursts (rate limit their concurrency to keep p95 sane).
 - Add tenant to allowlist for dedicated capacity if they buy reservation.

Ben (Support): I tried a quick repro from our side against production (tb-879 credentials). I could reproduce elevated p95 when the noisy embed job was running. When I forced requests to a sibling host (via debug routing), p95 dropped back to ~1.9s.

Rita (Infra): I temporarily applied a per-tenant concurrency cap for tb-879: max_concurrency=4 and a soft rate limit 15 rps. Config applied at 14:15 UTC. Monitoring now.

deploy-bot: "Applied config change: support/tenant-throttles -> tb-879 {max_concurrency:4, rate_limit_rps:15} (deployed by Rita)."

Sam (SRE): After cap applied, observed p95 returned to ~1.7s within two minutes. p99 still has occasional spikes up to 3.2s for very large prompts, likely due to KV cache cold starts. Suggest we enable prefix caching for tb-879 for 24h to reduce cache misses while we plan more stable mitigation.

Rita (Infra): Enabled short-term prefix/KV caching for tb-879 for 24h. Also flagged gpu-az3-11 to avoid scheduling embed-heavy batch jobs for the next 2 hours.

Alicia (CS): Communicated back to customer: we applied a temporary throttle and prefix caching. They replied "thanks, improved" and provided a fresh repro that now shows p95 ~1.6s. They've asked for a durable fix and wonder if we can guarantee isolation.

Ben (Support): Next steps suggested for customer-facing answer:
 - Offer an allowlist/reservation: reserved capacity (Dedicated) or soft guarantee on hosted pool (add to small-reservation pool) to avoid noisy neighbors. Sales handoff required for dedicated.
 - Documented config: increasing tenant weight or backing with dedicated pool reduces tail.
 - Provide best-practice prompt guidance: split long prompts, use prefix caching.

Sam (SRE): Internal follow-ups:
 - Create a cron to detect embed-batch jobs that saturate memory bandwidth and defer them if they coincide with latency-sensitive hosts.
 - Improve autoscheduler to consider KV cache heat and tenant affinity.
 - Potential enhancement: per-tenant placement constraints to avoid colocating embeddings and low-latency generation.

Rita (Infra): Filed infra ticket INF-5643 to add placement hints and to add a short-term heuristic to avoid scheduling big embed batches on hosts with low-latency tenants.

Alicia (CS): Customer wants a timeline for a durable solution. I'll offer: short-term throttle + caching (done), 24-48h monitoring + if they want guarantees, propose Dedicated/reservation — I'll loop in Sales.

Ben (Support): Closing note: keep thread updated if p99 resurges. If we see >2x baseline p99 for 3 consecutive 15-min windows, we'll roll back the host to maintenance and failover live traffic.

Sam (SRE): Acknowledged. I'm adding an automated alert rule to fire at 2x baseline p95/p99 for tenant tb-879 and tag the runbook for oncall.

Alicia (CS): Thanks all — customer happy for now. I'll follow up tomorrow with monitoring snapshots and the sales contact.

Rita (Infra): Monitoring: last check p95=1.62s, p99=2.98s. Leaving throttle & caching in place for 24h. Will escalate to Dedicated recommendation if we see recurring spikes.

Alicia (CS): Perfect — marking this resolved for now. If anything changes, re-open this thread.
